problem:
The size of a bush growing in a schoolyard is being monitored. The area $A\,{\text{m}}^{2}$ of the bush at any given moment grows at a rate that's directly proportional to the area at that moment. Additionally, $2\,{\text{m}}^{2}$ of the bush is cut away every month.
What is the differential equation that describes the rate of change in the area of the schoolyard bush at time $t,$ where $t$ is the time in months since it started growing?
worked_solution:
The rate of change in the area of the bush per month increases in proportion to $A$ and decreases by $2.$ The differential equation that describes this is

$$
\frac{\text{d}A}{\text{d}t}=kA-2,
$$

where $k$ is the (positive) constant of proportionality.
